scarborough.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit in Scarborough
s1loc: Scarborough's charity life leans on Saint Catherine's Hospice, whose donation hub on Queen Margaret's Road supplies a dozen shops across Falsgrave, Ramshill, Victoria Road and North Marine Road. Scarborough and District Foodbank works through local churches, while the big food-redistribution and foodbank networks, FareShare and Trussell, channel surplus and emergency parcels into the town. Tesco food collections call regularly for Scarborough volunteers, and Two Ridings Community Foundation backs grassroots projects right across this stretch of the North Yorkshire coast.

The sector here runs at every size. National and regional charities keep shops along Westborough and Newborough with central buying behind them, while small community groups, the one-room foodbank, mutual-aid pantries and volunteer-run projects work on a shoestring across Eastfield, Barrowcliff and the old town. Age UK and Scarborough Survivors sit alongside breakfast clubs and luncheon clubs fed by the redistribution networks. We are set up to serve the national charity and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts and direct online ordering, no minimum.

Beyond the hospice, Scarborough hosts the Rainbow Centre supporting people facing homelessness, the SeaChange Wave foodbank and Coast and Vale Community Action, the local volunteer-support body that helps small groups find people and funding. Charity shops cluster on Aberdeen Walk and Castle Road, raising money for everything from the RNLI lifeboat crews to local hospice care. Around Newby, Scalby and the harbourside, residents' associations and church-run pantries quietly keep neighbours fed, clothed and supported through the leaner winter months.

orpington.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit in Orpington
s1loc: Orpington anchors Bromley Borough Foodbank, run from Orpington Baptist Church on Station Road, which has handed out emergency parcels since 2010 and helped tens of thousands of local adults and children. Transform Bromley Borough runs a central food distribution hub in Orpington that stores dry, fresh and frozen stock for a dozen community food projects. The big food-redistribution and foodbank networks, FareShare and Trussell, feed the wider effort, while community fridges and church pantries keep the supply moving across the area.

The sector runs at every size in Orpington. National and regional charities hold shops along the High Street with central buying behind them, while small community groups, the one-room foodbank, pantries and volunteer-run projects work on a shoestring across Petts Wood, St Mary Cray, Crofton and Ramsden. Community Links Bromley supports the smaller groups, and breakfast clubs and luncheon clubs draw on the redistribution networks. Bromley's hospice, St Christopher's, runs charity shops reaching into Orpington and raises funds for end-of-life care across the borough. The Salvation Army keeps a presence locally, and mutual-aid groups that grew up around Petts Wood and Chelsfield still run shopping rounds and befriending for isolated neighbours. Charity shops along Orpington High Street back causes from air ambulance to children's services, while Bromley's volunteer centre helps residents in Green Street Green and Farnborough find roles with the groups that need them most.

wallasey.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit in Wallasey
s1loc: Wallasey sits at the heart of Wirral's charity effort. FareShare Merseyside and Wirral runs its base on Wheatland Lane in Wallasey, redistributing surplus food to more than a hundred charities and community groups, from breakfast clubs to refuges and luncheon clubs. Wirral Foodbank, with offices on Dock Road in nearby Birkenhead, keeps no-one going hungry across the peninsula, while Wirral Hospice St John's runs a charity shop in Wallasey Village. The big food-redistribution and foodbank networks, Trussell and FareShare, underpin the whole picture.

The sector runs at every size in Wallasey. Feeding Birkenhead and local social supermarkets stretch every donation. Beyond the hospice shops, Wallasey hosts community hubs and church pantries around Leasowe and Moreton, with Magenta Living and local housing groups backing food and welfare projects. Voluntary and Community Action Wirral supports smaller groups to find volunteers and funding, while charity shops in New Brighton raise money for everything from Claire House Children's Hospice to the RNLI. Mutual-aid networks built around Seacombe and Egremont still run shopping drops and befriending visits for older and isolated residents through the colder months.

hayes.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit in Hayes
s1loc: Hayes is served by Hillingdon Foodbank, which launched in 2009 as the first foodbank in London and runs distribution points including St Edmund's in Hayes from its base on New Windsor Street, Uxbridge. Around 176 volunteers keep it going, collecting from supermarkets, churches and schools, while the big food-redistribution and foodbank networks, Trussell and FareShare, supply the wider effort. The Salvation Army's Hillingbridge presence and Harlington Hospice both back food and welfare work for families in and around Hayes.

Uxbridge College and Brunel University students volunteer regularly, and community fridges stretch every donation. Harlington Hospice runs care and charity-shop fundraising reaching into Hayes, while local women's groups, DASH and church-run pantries support specific communities around Botwell and Yeading. Hillingdon AHWP and the borough's volunteer-support network help small groups recruit and train people, and charity shops along Station Road raise money for causes from children's services to air ambulance. Mutual-aid groups formed around Wood End and Townfield still run shopping rounds and befriending for older neighbours, keeping people connected through quieter spells.

Aylesbury Vineyard Storehouse helps people on low incomes with food, furniture and clothing, while Youth Concern runs a youth foodbank at its drop-in centre for 13 to 25 year-olds. s1loc: Hereford Food Bank, a charitable incorporated organisation run by a committee and a small staff team with a band of volunteers, provides seven-day emergency parcels across the city and surrounding county. Most of its food is donated by local people and businesses, backed by the big food-redistribution and foodbank networks, Trussell and FareShare. HVOSS, the Herefordshire Voluntary Organisations Support Service, guides volunteers and small community groups, while St Michael's Hospice anchors care and fundraising right across this rural corner of the West Midlands.

merthyr tydfil.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit in Merthyr Tydfil

FareShare Cymru, based near Cardiff, redistributes surplus food to charities and community groups across South Wales. Voluntary Action Merthyr Tydfil supports the town's smaller groups, while the Merthyr Tydfil Food Prosperity Network develops Affordable Food Clubs offering nutritious food at low cost to local families.

Charity shops along Merthyr's High Street raise money for causes from air ambulance to children's services, while community hubs around Treharris, Bedlinog and Troedyrhiw run pantries and befriending.
